title: The Honolulu contract with Johnny Mitchell
summary: Mitchell's band is offered a Honolulu job with a contract in which the band holds the option and any one man can veto staying.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: October 1926 I rejoined Johnny Mitchell who had an offer to go to Honolulu. I had just got back from San Franciso, I think it was about Thursday and he called me at my house--I called him to let him know I was in town, and I said I'm sleeping now because I drove all night from San Francisco, call me back this afternoon. And so he did. This was Thursday and he said they had a job to go to San Francisco--Honolulu--Saturday. I said what? He said yes, it's all made up with the tip and the
money, the contract is all signed. I said I have to think this over, give me another day to think a little bit. I just got here and my wife don't want me to leave right away again.
Anyway, I decided to go. In the band was myself, Gene Wright on piano, Lee Gibson on drums, C. L. Burke and myself on trumpet. Johnny had a contract, three months, with a three-month option.
We held the option, not the boss. If we wanted to work for another three months, we could; if we didn't we were free to come back home.
Also, any one man in the band could veto, and I was the veto. I didn't want to stay another three months so the whole band had to leave.
That was very interesting; that was some kind of contract, wasn't it, Mr. Blakeney?
in the contract that everybody had to agree to stay. If one man didn't want to stay, everybody had to leave.
On January 1, 1927 we caught the boat and came back to L.A.
